title: Network Attacks and Defence in Depth

questions.question: What distinguishes a DDoS attack from a simple DoS attack?
options: DDoS only targets websites, DoS only targets routers
DDoS uses one powerful machine, DoS uses many
DDoS floods the target from thousands of distributed sources at once
DDoS attacks encryption, DoS attacks firewalls
questions.rationale: A DDoS coordinates a botnet of many hijacked devices so the flood is distributed and far harder to block than a single-source DoS.

questions.question: A botnet is best described as:
options: A network of hijacked devices controlled by an attacker
A brand of firewall appliance
A protocol for encrypted DNS
A testing lab for malware samples
questions.rationale: Infected machines, cameras, and routers are remotely controlled as one army, each contributing small traffic that adds up to a flood.

questions.question: In a DNS amplification attack, the attacker sends small queries that trigger:
options: Large replies redirected to the victim using spoofed source addresses
Encrypted DNS tunnelling to the victim
Zone transfers to the attacker
Cache poisoning at the victim's resolver
questions.rationale: Open resolvers answer small queries with much larger responses aimed at the spoofed victim address, multiplying the attacker's bandwidth many times.

questions.question: Which defence most directly defeats man-in-the-middle interception of web traffic?
options: Rate limiting
TLS encryption with verified certificates
Longer passwords
MAC address filtering
questions.rationale: TLS makes intercepted traffic unreadable and authenticates the server via certificates, so an eavesdropper sees only ciphertext.

questions.question: What extra capability does a stateful firewall have over a simple packet-filtering firewall?
options: It encrypts outgoing packets
It tracks whole conversations in a state table
It blocks spam emails
It scans files for viruses
questions.rationale: Stateful firewalls remember established connections, so reply traffic to sessions you started passes automatically while unsolicited packets are dropped.

questions.question: A web application firewall (WAF) protects mainly at which layer?
options: Physical cabling
The HTTP application layer
The DNS root
The power supply
questions.rationale: A WAF inspects HTTP requests and payloads, filtering web attacks like injection and cross-site scripting before they reach the application.

questions.question: What is the practical difference between an IDS and an IPS?
options: An IDS blocks attacks inline, an IPS only watches
An IDS detects and alerts, an IPS sits inline and blocks
They are identical hardware with different logos
An IDS works on layer 1, an IPS on layer 7
questions.rationale: IDS monitors copies of traffic and raises alerts without touching the flow, while an IPS is placed inline and can stop malicious traffic in real time.

questions.question: The core idea of zero trust architecture is:
options: Trust everything inside the corporate firewall
Never trust, always verify — regardless of network location
Trust only devices with antivirus installed
Trust users but never administrators
questions.rationale: Zero trust removes implicit trust based on location: every request must be authenticated, authorised, and encrypted, whether it originates inside or outside the network.

questions.question: ARP poisoning on a local network is typically used to enable which attack?
options: Man in the middle interception
DNS amplification
Brute-force password cracking
Ransomware encryption
questions.rationale: By sending false ARP replies, the attacker associates their MAC with the gateway's address so local traffic flows through them for interception or tampering.

questions.question: On open public Wi-Fi, the primary benefit of connecting through a VPN is:
options: It hides your device brand from websites
It creates an encrypted tunnel that defeats local eavesdropping
It makes your laptop immune to malware
It increases your bandwidth
questions.rationale: The VPN tunnel encrypts traffic end to end to a gateway, so anyone sniffing the local network sees only unreadable ciphertext.
